key_insight: A training-free zero-shot framework can localize anomalies in 3D medical volumes by reusing 2D foundation models and comparing each subject’s tokens against other subjects for mutual similarity.
clinical_relevance: This could help flag unusual lesions in scans when labeled 3D training data are scarce, potentially supporting broader deployment across changing protocols and patient populations.
method: Decomposes each 3D volume along multiple anatomical axes and encodes slices with a frozen 2D vision transformer.
Pools neighboring slice features into localized volumetric tokens for cross-subject anomaly scoring.
Uses coarse-to-fine tokenization to better preserve focal lesion signals during depth pooling.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on brain MRI for metastases, glioma, and stroke, and also validated on lung CT to test generalizability beyond brain imaging.
watch_item: Fine tokenization may not help equally across modalities, and depth pooling can still attenuate small focal lesions if token resolution is too coarse.
paper_title: Toward Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in 3D Medical Images: A Batch-Based Approach Using 2D Foundation Models
